 BMW’s Previous Recall Failed to Fix Fire Risk, 720,796 Owners Now Told to Park Outside
 By: 
 Saajan Jogia 
 Published: 
 November 15, 2026 - 4:27 pm 
 Saajan Jogia 
 November 15, 2026 
 Add MotorBiscuit as a preferred source 
 BMW of North America is recalling 720,796 vehicles because of a fire risk that can persist even when they are parked and switched off. The affected models were previously recalled in 2024 for a water pump problem, but now require another repair.
 The National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) has advised affected owners in a press release to park their BMWs outside and away from buildings and other vehicles until the issue is addressed.
 According to the NHTSA recall report , the issue is related to the water pump electrical connector. Over time, material degradation of the connector could allow moisture to enter the pump, potentially causing a short circuit and fire. The affected BMW models are as follows:
 2012-2016 BMW 3 Series
 2012-2016 BMW 5 Series
 2012–2015 BMW X1
 2012-2016 BMW Z4
 2013-2017 BMW X3
 2014-2016 BMW 2 Series Coupe
 2014–2016 BMW 3 Series Sportswagon
 2014-2016 BMW 328i xDrive Gran Turismo
 2014-2016 BMW 4 Series convertible
 2014-2016 BMW 4 Series coupe
 2015-2016 BMW 2 Series convertible
 2015-2016 BMW 4 Series Gran Coupe
 2015-2018 BMW X4
 2016-2018 BMW X5 xDrive40e
 BMW’s previous recall, 24V-608, involved fitting a protective shield near the water pump and inspecting its electrical connector and wiring. Damaged pumps or wiring were replaced when necessary. However, further cases of overheating and thermal damage emerged, including vehicles that had already received the repair.
 Investigations in 2026 found cracks and localized embrittlement in the pump connectors, although the root cause remained undetermined. After reviewing the findings with its supplier, BMW announced recall 26V733 on October 28, 2026, covering 720,796 vehicles. The automaker reported approximately 10 related U.S. field incidents but no known crashes or injuries.
 BMW plans to begin notifying affected owners by mail on December 25, 2026. The same day, owners will be able to check their vehicles using their vehicle identification numbers (VINs) or license plate numbers through NHTSA’s recall lookup tool .
 For more information, owners can call BMW at 800-525-7417 or NHTSA at 888-327-4236. They can also use NHTSA’s SaferCar app to receive updates about vehicle recalls.
